title: feat(smtp): SQLite-backed persistent DNS record cache (SPF/DKIM/DMARC)
description:
## Why

The in-memory mail-auth cache (41l0) is empty after every restart. A sender like Gmail delivers thousands of messages over days; every restart re-fetches and re-parses the same DKIM key and SPF policy from DNS. SQLite as a persistent backing store gives restart resilience and an audit trail at zero infrastructure cost.

## Design

Two-tier cache:

```
[DNS wire]
    ↓  (on cache miss in both tiers)
raw TXT bytes ──→ SQLite: dns_records(fqdn, record_type, raw BLOB, valid_until INTEGER)
                              ↓  (on hit)
              in-memory DashMap: fqdn → (Arc<Txt>, Instant)   ← from 41l0
```

### Schema (new migration in stoa-smtp or stoa-verify)

```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS dns_records (
    fqdn        TEXT    NOT NULL,
    record_type TEXT    NOT NULL,   -- "TXT", "MX", "A", "AAAA", "PTR"
    raw         BLOB    NOT NULL,   -- raw serialized record bytes
    valid_until INTEGER NOT NULL,   -- Unix seconds (from DNS TTL)
    fetched_at  INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime("%s","now")),
    PRIMARY KEY (fqdn, record_type)
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_dns_records_expiry ON dns_records (valid_until);
```

### Cache struct

```rust
pub struct DnsRecordCache {
    pool: SqlitePool,
    hot:  DashMap<(Box<str>, RecordType), (Arc<Txt>, Instant)>,
}
```

Implements `mail_auth::ResolverCache<Box<str>, Txt>`:
- `get(fqdn)`: check hot map first (Instant expiry); on miss check SQLite (valid_until > now()); on SQLite hit deserialize bytes, populate hot map, return
- `insert(fqdn, value, valid_until)`: write to hot map AND SQLite synchronously (or spawn a blocking task for the SQLite write to avoid blocking the async path)
- `remove(fqdn)`: evict from both tiers

### Wire-in

In `crates/smtp/src/server.rs`, construct `Arc<DnsRecordCache>` at startup (alongside `MessageAuthenticator`). Clone into each session. Pass to `verify_inbound` as a parameter. In `auth.rs` `verify_inbound`, attach via `.with_txt_cache(&cache)` on `SpfParameters`, `DkimParameters`, `DmarcParameters`.

### Expiry / hygiene

- Hot map: checked on every `get` via `Instant`; expired entries return None and are removed
- SQLite: a startup sweep `DELETE FROM dns_records WHERE valid_until < strftime("%s","now")` removes stale rows; no background task needed
- No GC worker required — expired rows are harmless dead weight until the next startup sweep

### Serialization format

`Txt` from mail-auth is `Vec<Vec<u8>>` (list of TXT strings). Serialize as length-prefixed concatenation or JSON array of base64 strings. Use a simple canonical format; this is internal-only, not wire-protocol.

## What stays the same

- Per-connection concurrency model unchanged
- hickory-resolver DNS-level cache unchanged
- `verify_inbound` signature changes minimally (one extra `&DnsRecordCache` param)

## Acceptance criteria

- After process restart, a previously-seen DKIM selector is served from SQLite without a DNS round-trip (verified by a test that pre-populates SQLite and asserts no DNS call is made)
- `get` on an expired SQLite row returns None
- `insert` writes to both tiers atomically enough that a crash-restart scenario still finds the row in SQLite
- Existing SPF/DKIM/DMARC tests pass unchanged
- cargo fmt + clippy -D warnings + cargo test --workspace all pass clean
design:
spawn_blocking for SQLite writes: mail-auth calls insert() from async context; use tokio::task::spawn_blocking (or sqlx's own async execute) rather than blocking the tokio task. Same pattern as LMDB writes elsewhere in the codebase.

Serialization: serde_json over Vec<Vec<u8>> with base64-encoded inner vecs. Human-readable in the DB, trivially debuggable with sqlite3, no custom format to maintain.
